assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection into exporting reshaped international trade theory and empirics. It explains within-industry reallocation and gains from trade beyond the representative-firm and new-trade-theory frameworks. It has a very large downstream literature and policy relevance.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central model. Helpman is credited for the broader heterogeneous-firm and trade-structure agenda, including Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple on exports versus FDI. Redding is influential in quantitative and spatial extensions, but I treat those as a later wave of the programme.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of confirmation across firm-level data and many countries. The framework is canonical in graduate teaching and empirical work.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers to credit Melitz alone or with Helpman, and whether other contributors (e.g. Bernard, Eaton, Jensen, Kortum) merit inclusion.
Another trade-field prize may be seen as too soon after Krugman (2008).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework, with nominal rigidities, staggered pricing and rule-based monetary policy, is the dominant workhorse of central-bank analysis. Its impact on both macroeconomic theory and policy practice is very large.
assessment.attribution: Credit is highly diffuse across eight names. Calvo contributed staggered pricing, Taylor the staggered-contract and interest-rate-rule work, and Woodford the systematic synthesis and welfare-based policy analysis. Gali, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets contributed in other important ways. Any three-person selection leaves out major contributors.
assessment.maturity: Decades of use in policy institutions. The framework has been tested and criticised through the financial crisis and the post-pandemic inflation, and has been extended rather than abandoned.
uncertainties: Attribution is inherently contested and the three-name limit is binding.
Parts of the framework are criticised empirically (e.g. the Phillips curve in recent inflation episodes).
Lucas, Sargent, Prescott and others have already been recognised for neighbouring macro advances.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Kiyotaki-Moore (1997) credit cycles and the Bernanke-Gertler-Gilchrist financial accelerator formalised how collateral constraints amplify and propagate shocks. They became the foundation for post-2008 macro-financial modelling and policy discussion.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore for the collateral-constraint mechanism. Gertler for the financial accelerator and its later quantitative DSGE integration. Gilchrist is an important empirical and quantitative contributor. Bernanke, who shares the accelerator, already holds the prize, which complicates the group.
assessment.maturity: Roughly three decades of evidence and extension, with renewed relevance after 2008. The literature has been used heavily in policy and macroprudential debates.
uncertainties: Gertler also appears in the New Keynesian group, so credit overlaps across candidates.
Bernanke's prior award and the Diamond-Dybvig-Bernanke 2022 recognition may reduce the appetite for another financial-frictions prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Modern political economics uses formal models and comparative data to analyse how electoral rules, constitutions, state capacity and fiscal institutions shape policy outcomes. It is a coherent, widely used research programme that links economics with political science.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini are the central figures through their electoral-rule and constitutional work, including their 2000 and 2003 books. Besley is closely associated with state capacity, political accountability and development. The grouping is credible, but some contributions overlap with earlier work in public choice and political science.
assessment.maturity: Established over 25 years. The empirical identification behind some of the constitutional results is weaker than in the best natural-experiment literatures.
uncertainties: Persson's connection to the Academy and the Stockholm IIES community may be a disclosed conflict that the committee would need to handle.
The 2024 prize on institutions may make another institutions-related award seem repetitive.
Causal evidence on constitutions and electoral rules is contested.
My own field proximity risks bias.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mian and Sufi show with granular data that household leverage and credit supply expansions drive booms, busts and weak recoveries. This changed how economists and policymakers view household debt and financial crises.
assessment.attribution: The core contributions, including 'House of Debt', the credit-supply and housing-wealth work, and the follow-on papers, are clearly attributable to the two of them. Campbell is a major finance economist but his work is less specific to this discovery.
assessment.maturity: The work dates mainly from 2009 to 2017, so it is about 10 to 15 years old. That is mature enough to judge, though it is on the early side and the long-run verdict is still forming.
uncertainties: The work is relatively recent and may be viewed as too early.
Replication and interpretation debates exist about credit-supply versus demand explanations in the 2000s boom.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The elasticity-of-taxable-income approach and the sufficient-statistics approach to optimal taxation connect theory directly to behavioural evidence and shape tax-policy analysis. Their effect on public finance practice is substantial.
assessment.attribution: Saez is central across theory and empirics. Slemrod is a leading figure in the taxable-income and tax-compliance literature. Feldstein, the originator of the ETI idea, is deceased. Chetty and Stantcheva are important but are better assessed on other bodies of work.
assessment.maturity: More than 20 years of work, with sustained evaluation and debate over the size and interpretation of the elasticities.
uncertainties: Saez appears in several candidate groups, which fragments his credit.
The size of the elasticities and the credibility of identification remain disputed.
Feldstein's priority cannot be rewarded posthumously.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The intertemporal approach to the open economy ('new open-economy macroeconomics'), the exchange-rate disconnect puzzles and the 'six major puzzles' framing shaped modern international macroeconomics. The textbook and papers have a lasting influence on research and policy.
assessment.attribution: Obstfeld and Rogoff are the clear joint pair for the Foundations of International Macroeconomics and the Redux model (with Rogoff). Some overlapping credit goes to Sachs, Svensson and others.
assessment.maturity: Established over 30 years. The empirical resolution of the puzzles is incomplete.
uncertainties: Rogoff appears in a second candidate group, B005, on financial crises.
Many puzzles remain unresolved, which may make the discovery look like a research agenda rather than a settled result.
Mundell and Krugman have already been recognised for related open-economy work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Hsieh and Klenow (2009) provided a tractable, data-based framework showing that misallocation across firms can account for a large part of cross-country income differences in TFP. It linked micro-level frictions to development and growth and produced a large empirical literature.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow are the principal authors of the measurement framework. Restuccia, with Rogerson, who is not listed, contributed the closely related theoretical and quantitative argument. The credit division therefore has some ambiguity.
assessment.maturity: About 15 or more years old and widely used. The magnitude of the estimated gains is sensitive to measurement and has been challenged on data and model-specification grounds.
uncertainties: Measurement-error and model-dependence critiques may weaken the quantitative claims.
Rogerson's absence from the credited names makes the attribution incomplete.
The policy implications are less direct than in some other candidates.
